transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I keep forgetting everyday things—appointments, errands, even important family plans—and it’s starting to cause problems at home. It has been causing some tension with my husband lately because he feels like he can't rely on me for our family logistics.
Have you noticed any other changes in your behavior or mood, such as feeling sad, anxious, or irritable, alongside these memory issues?

I don't really feel depressed or anxious, though I do feel quite frustrated and stressed about how my forgetfulness and organizational struggles are impacting my life. It is just hard when my mistakes start causing tension at home.
Have you recently started or increased your use of alcohol or any substances that could be contributing to your memory issues?
No, not at all. I don't use any substances and only have an occasional glass of wine, so that definitely isn't the cause of my memory and focus issues.
Can you tell me more about when you first noticed these memory issues and if they have been progressively getting worse over time?

These issues actually go back to childhood—my elementary school teachers always wrote that I was bright but constantly daydreaming and forgetting my homework. They didn't necessarily get worse on their own, but they became unmanageable about 18 months ago when I stepped back from my structured consulting work. Without those rigid schedules and lists keeping me on track, my coping mechanisms just fell apart.
You mentioned daydreaming in elementary school, can you tell me more about what you mean by daydreaming, was it difficulty paying attention in class or something else?

Yes, it was definitely a struggle with paying attention and staying focused in class. My teachers often wrote on my report cards that I was bright but constantly daydreaming, chatting, and forgetting to turn in homework I'd actually finished. My parents even used to joke that I was always "off in my own world" instead of finishing my chores.
Did you also experience excessive restlessness, fidgeting, or an inability to sit still, especially during your childhood, alongside the difficulty with paying attention and forgetfulness?

Currently, I definitely struggle with that—I constantly fidget by bouncing my leg or tapping my pen, and sitting still for more than half an hour makes me feel incredibly restless. But as a child, it wasn't really physical hyperactivity; back then, it was much more about daydreaming, chatting, and being "off in my own world" instead of doing my chores.

Can you tell me more about how your symptoms have impacted your daily life and relationships, particularly in terms of following through on instructions, making careless mistakes, or avoiding tasks that require mental effort?

It has had a major impact; I often make careless mistakes, like misreading lines or leaving out entire expense columns on our neighborhood garden budget. I also struggle to follow through on tasks, so things like our mortgage refinance paperwork end up half-finished on my desk for weeks. This, along with missing school meetings and soccer pickups, has really strained my relationship with my husband because he feels he can't rely on me for family logistics.
Can you describe how often you experience impulsivity, such as interrupting others, blurting out answers, or difficulty waiting for your turn in conversations?

I struggle with this quite frequently. During family conversations or community garden meetings, I often blurt out my ideas before people finish their sentences or cut in with questions. I also get incredibly impatient and antsy waiting in lines, like at the farmers' market or the DMV, and have to stop myself from jumping ahead.
